name: Shou Puer

origin.subregion: fermented in factories across the province

categoryNote: Chinese 黑茶, “black tea”, is not English black tea (红茶). Puer’s relationship to the dark class is contested; this atlas files it here by process.

transformation.note: 渥堆 — a wet microbial pile. One of the most transformed teas in the atlas, whatever the oxidation scalar says.

processing.description: Same sha qing as sheng. The fork has not happened yet.
Maocha, 晒青, as for sheng.
Piled, watered, and turned for weeks — accelerated fermentation invented in the 1970s. This is the hatch on the chart.

profile.mouthfeel: thick, low astringency when well fermented and rested

rinses.notes: rinse is almost mandatory on young shou

decoction.when: after the gongfu session, or as a separate pot
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — simmer the spent leaf. Dark teas can take a boil; this is the extra cup the name 第四泡 points at.

water.note: Boiling. Shou can handle high leaf and many steeps.

storage: Air a new shou a few weeks if it smells like fish or pond; then airtight-ish, dry.

shelfLife.note: Most teas are food. A few teas are projects.

summary: Pile-fermented “ripe” puer: date, cocoa, and thickness without a decade of waiting.

compare.differentiator: Same sun-dried leaf until 渥堆. Sheng skipped the pile.
